subject: Service availability terms — pilot SLA proposal and credit structure
messages:
From: Janelle Park <janelle.park@finworks.com>
To: aditya_rao@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@finworks.com, Mark Goodwin <mgoodwin@finworks.com>
Date: Thu, 10 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: SLA template review and carveout asks for pilot

Aditya,

Thanks again for last week's demo — the latency profile looked promising for our chat routing use case. Procurement and engineering reviewed Redwood's standard SLA and we have a few asks before we can move the pilot forward:

- Availability target: our security and compliance team is asking whether you can commit to 99.5% uptime instead of 99.9% for the initial contract term (we're sensitive to predictable credits vs big variability).
- Monthly credit cap: we want a hard cap on monthly service credits (proposed: credits up to the full monthly invoice, but no more than 200% of the monthly fee).
- Maintenance carveouts: we need scheduled maintenance windows to be excluded from uptime calculations if notified 72 hours in advance and scheduled in a 4-hour window, maximum twice per month.
- Latency SLOs: can you add a p95 500ms target for our routed requests?

I've attached our annotated copy with preferred language (FinWorks_SLA_comments.docx). Can you share a version we can sign or a counter-proposal? Our procurement deadline for the pilot is EOD Sep 17.

Best,
Janelle Park
Director, Procurement | FinWorks
J: +1 415-555-0192

[attachment: FinWorks_SLA_comments.docx]

From: aditya_rao@redwood.ai
To: Janelle Park <janelle.park@finworks.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai, Mark Goodwin <mgoodwin@finworks.com>
Date: Fri, 11 Sep 2026 10:35:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SLA template review and carveout asks for pilot

Janelle — thanks for the clear notes and the annotated doc. Appreciate the timeline. I reviewed your asks with our CS and legal leads. High level response and a proposed compromise below — attaching a Redwood counter (SLA_Template_v3.pdf) and a short metrics export (redwood_uptime_metrics.csv) for the last 12 months across accounts similar to your scale.

Quick summary (proposal):
- Availability target: Redwood standard is 99.9% monthly availability. For the pilot we can offer a phased availability commitment: 99.8% for the first 3 months, moving to 99.9% after the pilot if usage and routing patterns align.
- Monthly service credit ladder: we propose a graduated credit table tied to monthly availability bands (see SLA_Template_v3.pdf). Credit payout is capped at 150% of the monthly invoice in any billing period for the pilot, with a bilateral review at the pilot endpoint.
- Maintenance carveouts: we can accept scheduled maintenance carveouts if Redwood provides 72 hours notice and limits work to a single 4‑hour window per scheduled event. We cannot commit to unlimited twice-per-month exclusions — instead we propose up to two scheduled events per quarter for infrastructure upgrades that require service-level carveouts (we'll provide calendar invites).
- Latency SLOs: we can include a p95 latency target of 400–500ms for routed inference requests in the pilot profile, with an operational playbook to troubleshoot regressions.

We think the phased availability plus the 150% cap is a practical middle ground that balances predictability for you and operational flexibility for us during the pilot. Next steps: if this looks viable, I'll loop in Laura (legal) for a redline pass and Monica (CS) for the operational checklist. Also happy to jump on a quick 30-min call to walk through the credit table.

Action items:
- Janelle: confirm whether FinWorks can accept the phased availability path (99.8% → 99.9% after pilot).
- Aditya: produce redline-ready doc (attached) and metrics export.

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Account Executive — Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
aditya_rao@redwood.ai | +1 650-555-0167

[attachments: SLA_Template_v3.pdf, redwood_uptime_metrics.csv]

From: procurement@finworks.com
To: aditya_rao@redwood.ai
Cc: Janelle Park <janelle.park@finworks.com>, Mark Goodwin <mgoodwin@finworks.com>
Date: Mon, 13 Sep 2026 08:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SLA template review and carveout asks for pilot

Aditya / Redwood team,

Thanks for the quick turnaround and the data. We reviewed the proposed middle ground with engineering and legal. A couple of points that still matter for us:

1) Availability baseline: 99.8% for the pilot is an improvement on our ask but still less than our preferred 99.5 floor? To clarify — we originally asked for a permanent 99.5% (lower than Redwood's standard) because we value a predictable credit model. Your phased approach is acceptable only if the credit economics are close to what we asked.

2) Credit cap: 150% cap is lower than our requested 200% cap. Procurement needs an absolute cap at 200% of monthly charges for the pilot to get internal approval.

3) Maintenance carveouts: engineering will accept Redwood's quarterly carveout approach if you confirm that emergency maintenance (hotfixes) will never be scheduled without confirmed notice unless a P0 incident is being fixed.

4) DocuSign / timeline: we need a contract we can sign by Sep 17 to lock the pilot.

We've added inline comments in your SLA_Template_v3.pdf and re-attached our annotated doc (FinWorks_SLA_comments.docx) with a suggested replacement clause for monthly cap and emergency maintenance language. If Redwood can accept the 200% cap for the pilot and agree to emergency-work guardrails, procurement will fast-track sign-off.

Regards,
FinWorks Procurement Team
procurement@finworks.com

[attachment: FinWorks_SLA_comments.docx]

From: aditya_rao@redwood.ai
To: Janelle Park <janelle.park@finworks.com>, procurement@finworks.com
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 15:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SLA template review and carveout asks for pilot

Janelle — procurement team, thanks for the clear feedback and the annotated file. Looping in Laura (Head of Legal) and Monica (Customer Success) to close the remaining points. My read and recommended compromise below so we can hit your Sep 17 pilot start:

Proposed final terms for pilot (Redwood counter):
- Availability: 99.8% monthly for the first 6 months of the pilot agreement (we lengthened the ramp to 6 months to give ops time to tune traffic shaping and caching). After month 6 we'll re-evaluate and transition to 99.9% if agreed metrics are met.
- Monthly service credit cap: we will accept a 200% cap of the monthly invoice for the pilot only, with a mutual review at the end of the pilot to settle longer-term caps.
- Maintenance carveouts: scheduled maintenance will be excluded from uptime if Redwood provides 72 hours notice and schedules work in a single 4-hour window. Emergency maintenance (hotfixes) will not be scheduled proactively without notice; if an emergency change is required to address a P0 customer-impacting issue, Redwood will notify FinWorks within 1 hour and provide a post‑incident summary within 48 hours.
- Latency SLO: include p95 <= 500ms for routed inference during business hours (8am–8pm PT), with an operational escalation playbook owned by Monica.
- Credit mechanics: credits are measured and applied monthly; claims must be submitted within 30 days of invoice. Credits issued reduce future invoices — we will not automatically pay out cash for pilot credits.

Attachments and next steps: Laura, please review the attached SLA redline and confirm we're OK to accept the 200% cap for pilot. Monica, please prepare the operational runbook and an onboarding checklist for Sep 20–24. Janelle / procurement: if this is acceptable, I'll upload the redline to DocuSign and share the link for signatures today so we can start the pilot on Sep 20.

If anyone prefers a 20-minute call to resolve the last legal bits, I'm available this afternoon.

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Account Executive — Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
aditya_rao@redwood.ai | +1 650-555-0167
